newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps soar, mogas up $5, CFDs backwardate.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps soar, mogas up $5, CFDs backwardate.

text.p: European oil swaps firmed on Monday led higher by Brent crude futures which levered further into backwardation on fears of a thin loading programme for North Sea crudes in June.
Brent crude CFDs jumped 15 cents a barrel to talk close to five cents over July for this week's dates while the next three weeks were backwardated by about four or five cents a week.
The 27-30 May week traded three cents above the 2-6 June week but no outright trades were heard. Despite the backwardation on weekly CFDs, monthly CFDs priced against the IPE remained in contango.
June was valued at 13 cents under the screen while July was nearer eight cents.
Gasoline gained $5 a tonne to talk around $203 for both May and June. July was $4.25 a tonne lower and physical barges traded from $197.50 to $202.50.
Crack spreads were unchanged at $4.10 a barrel and $3.10 for the third and fourth quarters respectively.
Heavy fuel also firmed $1 a tonne to $87 for May barges but little trade was heard. June was seen at parity with low sulphur holding some $6 a tonne higher.
Dealers said the strength largely reflected gains made in recent days in Singapore. Local demand for bunker fuel and from Italy for low sulphur were subdued.
Further forward the contango showed signs of flattening out. The third to fourth quarter contango fell to $4 a tonne from $5.50 last Wednesday.

Jet premiums stayed depressed after sinking $1 to $2 a tonne on Friday. June and July held at $20 a tonne and $22 a tonne above the IPE respectively. While the winter months were still pegged at $29 above the screen, having traded that level on Friday.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98). -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
